hints: Queries include creating a copy of the current array version, point updates, and range sums.
Use a persistent segment tree: each update creates new nodes only along one root-to-leaf path.
Keep one root per version; copying a version copies only its root pointer.
analogy: A copied version shares unchanged tree branches and gets fresh nodes only where a value changes.
example: Copy version 1 to version 2; changing position 3 in version 2 leaves version 1's value unchanged.
algorithm: Build an initial persistent sum tree. Copy operations append the same root; point updates path-copy nodes and assign the new root to that version; range queries use the selected root.
correctness: Every root describes its own full array because changed paths are copied while all unchanged intervals remain shared and identical.
complexity: O(log n) new nodes per update, O(log n) per query, O(n+u log n) memory for u updates.
